title: Quarterly roadmap: Adaptive Reservation Tiers pilot for Dedicated capacity (reduce cold-starts, test tiered economics)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We will run a quarter-long pilot of a new "Adaptive Reservation Tiers" product for Dedicated capacity: a small set of configurable reservation tiers (Reserved-Warm, Reserved-Cold, and On-DemandFallback) that trade capacity guarantees, prewarm behavior, eviction rules, and pricing. The goal is to reduce cold-start tail latency for dedicated customers while limiting fragmentation and overall unit cost.

Background & motivation:
- Customers using Dedicated pools report intermittent P95/P99 latency spikes due to cold KV cache misses and slow model load during sudden surges. Current options (fixed reserved pools or pure on-demand) are blunt instruments.
- We believe a tiered reservation model that pairs a small warm footprint with cheaper cold reservations and an on-demand fallback can: (1) improve tail latency for spiky workloads, (2) provide clearer pricing trade-offs for customers, and (3 reduce emergency overprovisioning.

Primary goals for the quarter:
1) Implement reservation tier primitives in the provisioning API and console so teams can opt into Warm/Cold/On-Demand tiers per-pool.
2) Add autoscaler policies and eviction rules that respect tier affinity and fairness (e.g., warm tenants get soft preemption protection; cold tiers can be reclaimed first).
3) Ship telemetry (tenant-level cold-start metrics, prewarm utilization, cross-tenant eviction traces) and a dashboard for pilot partners.
4) Run a 6–8 week pilot with 3 customers (mix of enterprise + AI-native) to validate latency and cost impacts and iterate on pricing.

Success metrics (quantitative):
- Reduce Dedicated P95 generation latency for pilot tenants by >= 30% under surge profiles.
- Maintain aggregate cost-per-token delta <= +10% (target neutral to slightly better).
- Eviction incidents impacting SLO-critical tenants < 1 per month during pilot.
- Pilot partners report "useful" or "very useful" for choice of tiers in follow-up survey (>= 3/4 positive).

Deliverables & acceptance criteria:
- API: new field "reservation_tier" on pool creation/update with documented semantics and validation. (AC: swagger entry + SDK flag + e2e tests)
- Console: UI for selecting tier with explainer and estimated cost delta. (AC: UX review sign-off + analytics capture)
- Autoscaler: policy knobs for min_warm_replicas, cold_eviction_score, and fast-fail fallback logic. (AC: unit + integration tests, runbook update)
- Telemetry: dashboards and alerting; histogram of cold-start latency by tenant, heatmap for eviction events, utilization metrics. (AC: dashboard link + alert runbook)
- Pilot plan: customer list, contact owners, SLA guardrails, and billing experiment plan. (AC: signed pilot agreements + weekly check-ins scheduled)

Timeline (quarter slice):
- Weeks 1–3: Design & API spec (PM + Eng + Design workshops), PRD and pricing experiment definition.
- Weeks 4–6: Platform implementation (provisioning API, autoscaler policy hooks, simple console flow).
- Weeks 7–8: Telemetry + dashboards + internal canary on low-risk tenants.
- Weeks 9–12: External pilot with first customers, iterate on policies and pricing; prepare post-pilot analysis.

Risks & mitigations:
- Capacity fragmentation: track utilization and enforce soft quotas; if fragmentation rises > 15% we will throttle cold reservations and revert pilot knobs.
- Customer confusion about tiers: include clear explainer copy and an interactive cost estimator in the console; run onboarding sessions.
- Evictions hitting critical workloads: implement preemption grace windows and automatic rollback to on-demand fallback.
- Telemetry noise: use synthetic canaries to validate signals before trusting production dashboards.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Aisha Patel (owner)
- ENG leads: Marco Nguyen (assignee), Priya Shah (autoscale), Lucas Romero (runtime)
- Design: Emma Chao (console flows)
- Sales / Customer Success: Rajiv Menon (pilot coordination)

Notes on pricing experiment:
- Default pilot pricing will credit early adopter customers for incremental cost during the pilot with a simple per-hour discount band for warm reservations. Billing changes will be surfaced as labels in billing exports and a pilot line-item in invoices.
